Section 613(b). Percentage depletion rates of 22, 15, 14, 10, 7.5, and 5 percent by named mineral, hitPolicy "first" so an earlier (higher-paragraph) row wins for a mineral named in more than one paragraph — reproducing the statute's own "if paragraph X does not apply" priority. The final catch-all row (14 percent) covers BOTH (b)(3)'s "metal mines... if paragraph (1)(B) or (2)(A) does not apply" residual and (b)(7)'s expressly non-exhaustive "all other minerals" residual: the two are legally distinct categories but numerically the same rate, so one catch-all row reproduces the computed outcome for both. NOT modelled: the "if from deposits in the United States" domestic gate on paragraphs (1)(B) and (2) (assumed satisfied), the (b)(7) rip-rap/ballast/road-material 5-percent carve-out, and clay/shale used for sewer pipe, brick, or lightweight aggregate at 7.5 percent under (b)(5) (both names collide with the plain "Clay"/"Shale" catch-all use and are recorded as TECH-GAPS G321 rather than guessed).
